Let \(p=503\). We want to determine for how many \(r\in\{0,1,\dots,501\}\),

\[
S_r=\sum_{m\ge 0}\binom{10000}{502m+r}
\]

is divisible by \(503\).

Write \(10000\) in base \(503\):

\[
10000=19\cdot 503+443.
\]

Now write any \(k\) as

\[
k=503a+b,\qquad 0\le b\le 502.
\]

By Lucas’s theorem,

\[
\binom{10000}{k}
=\binom{19\cdot 503+443}{a\cdot 503+b}
\equiv \binom{19}{a}\binom{443}{b}\pmod{503}.
\]

This congruence is nonzero only when

\[
0\le a\le 19,\qquad 0\le b\le 443.
\]

Also, since \(503\equiv 1\pmod{502}\),

\[
k=503a+b\equiv a+b\pmod{502}.
\]

Thus modulo \(503\),

\[
S_r\equiv \sum_{\substack{0\le a\le 19\\0\le b\le 443\\a+b\equiv r\pmod{502}}}
\binom{19}{a}\binom{443}{b}.
\]

But \(a+b\le 19+443=462<502\). Therefore the congruence \(a+b\equiv r\pmod{502}\) is possible only when \(r\le 462\), and then it means \(a+b=r\).

So for \(0\le r\le 462\),

\[
S_r\equiv \sum_{a+b=r}\binom{19}{a}\binom{443}{b}
=\binom{462}{r}\pmod{503}
\]

by Vandermonde’s identity.

Since \(462<503\), none of the binomial coefficients \(\binom{462}{r}\) are divisible by \(503\). Hence \(S_r\not\equiv 0\pmod{503}\) for \(0\le r\le 462\).

For \(r=463,464,\dots,501\), there are no possible pairs \((a,b)\), so

\[
S_r\equiv 0\pmod{503}.
\]

There are

\[
501-463+1=39
\]

such values.

Let \(p=503\). We want to know for how many \(r\in\{0,1,\dots,501\}\),

\[
S_r=\sum_{m\ge 0}\binom{10000}{502m+r}
\]

is divisible by \(503\).

Define the polynomial over \(\mathbb F_{503}\):

\[
Q(x)=\sum_{r=0}^{501} S_r x^r.
\]

For any nonzero \(x\in \mathbb F_{503}\), we have \(x^{502}=1\), so

\[
Q(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{10000}\binom{10000}{k}x^{k\bmod 502}
=\sum_{k=0}^{10000}\binom{10000}{k}x^k
=(1+x)^{10000}.
\]

Now \(10000\equiv 462\pmod{502}\). Thus for \(x\neq -1\),

\[
(1+x)^{10000}=(1+x)^{462}.
\]

At \(x=-1\), both sides are \(0\), so this also holds. Therefore for every nonzero \(x\in\mathbb F_{503}\),

\[
Q(x)=(1+x)^{462}.
\]

Both polynomials have degree at most \(501\), and they agree at all \(502\) nonzero elements of \(\mathbb F_{503}\). Hence they are identical modulo \(503\):

\[
Q(x)\equiv (1+x)^{462}\pmod{503}.
\]

So

\[
S_r\equiv \binom{462}{r}\pmod{503}
\]

for \(0\le r\le 462\), and

\[
S_r\equiv 0\pmod{503}
\]

for \(463\le r\le 501\).

Since \(462<503\), none of the binomial coefficients \(\binom{462}{r}\) is divisible by \(503\). Thus the only multiples of \(503\) occur for

\[
r=463,464,\dots,501,
\]

which gives

\[
501-463+1=39.
\]

Let \(p=503\), so \(p-1=502\). Work modulo \(503\).

For each \(r\), define

\[
A_r=\sum_{x\in \mathbb F_{503}^*} x^{-r}(1+x)^{10000}.
\]

Expanding,

\[
A_r=\sum_{k=0}^{10000}\binom{10000}{k}\sum_{x\in \mathbb F_{503}^*}x^{k-r}.
\]

Now

\[
\sum_{x\in \mathbb F_{503}^*}x^{k-r}
=
\begin{cases}
502\equiv -1 \pmod{503}, & k\equiv r \pmod{502},\\
0, & k\not\equiv r \pmod{502}.
\end{cases}
\]

Therefore,

\[
A_r\equiv -S_r \pmod{503}.
\]

Next, since

\[
10000\equiv 462 \pmod{502},
\]

we have for every \(x\in\mathbb F_{503}^*\),

\[
(1+x)^{10000}=(1+x)^{462},
\]

with \(x=-1\) also giving \(0\) on both sides. Hence

\[
A_r=\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_{503}^*}x^{-r}(1+x)^{462}.
\]

Expanding again,

\[
A_r=\sum_{j=0}^{462}\binom{462}{j}\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_{503}^*}x^{j-r}.
\]

Thus

\[
A_r\equiv
\begin{cases}
-\binom{462}{r}, & 0\le r\le 462,\\
0, & 463\le r\le 501.
\end{cases}
\]

So

\[
S_r\equiv
\begin{cases}
\binom{462}{r}, & 0\le r\le 462,\\
0, & 463\le r\le 501.
\end{cases}
\pmod{503}.
\]

Since \(462<503\), none of the binomial coefficients \(\binom{462}{r}\) are divisible by \(503\). Therefore the multiples of \(503\) occur exactly for

\[
r=463,464,\dots,501.
\]

There are

\[
501-463+1=39
\]

such integers.

\[

\[
S_r\equiv \sum_{a+b=r}\binom{19}{b}\binom{443}{a}

\[

\[
x^{502}=1.

\[
10000=19\cdot 502+462.

\[
A(x)\equiv (1+x)^{462}\pmod{503}.

\[
A(x)-(1+x)^{462}
\]

has degree at most \(501\), but it has all \(502\) nonzero elements of \(\mathbb F_{503}\) as roots. Therefore it must be the zero polynomial modulo \(503\). Hence

\[
A(x)\equiv (1+x)^{462}\pmod{503}.

S_r\equiv \binom{462}{r}\pmod{503}

\[
S_r\equiv 0\pmod{503}

\[
(1+x)^{503}\equiv 1+x^{503}\pmod{503}.

\[
(1+x)^{10000}
=
(1+x)^{19\cdot 503+443}
\equiv
(1+x^{503})^{19}(1+x)^{443}.

\[
(1+x)^{10000}\equiv (1+x)^{19}(1+x)^{443}=(1+x)^{462}.

\[
S_r\equiv \binom{462}{r}\pmod{503}

S_r\equiv 0\pmod{503}

Since the pentagon is equiangular, each exterior angle is \(72^\circ\).

Each diagonal is formed by two adjacent sides, so

\[
\sum d_i^2=\sum \left(x_i^2+x_{i+1}^2+2x_ix_{i+1}\cos72^\circ\right).
\]

Thus

\[
800=2S+2A\cos72^\circ.
\]

\[
800=616+2A\cos72^\circ,
\]

so

\[
2A\cos72^\circ=184.

\[
0=S+2A\cos72^\circ+2B\cos144^\circ.
\]

Therefore

\[
0=308+184+2B\cos144^\circ,
\]

so

\[
2B\cos144^\circ=-492.
\]

Now

\[
\cos72^\circ=\frac{\sqrt5-1}{4},\qquad \cos144^\circ=-\frac{\sqrt5+1}{4}.
\]

Hence

\[
A=\frac{92}{\cos72^\circ}=92(\sqrt5+1),

\[
B=\frac{-246}{\cos144^\circ}=246(\sqrt5-1).

\[
P^2=S+2A+2B.
\]

Thus

\[
P^2=308+2\cdot 92(\sqrt5+1)+2\cdot 246(\sqrt5-1).
\]

Simplifying,

\[
P^2=676\sqrt5.
\]

\[
